papers.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
reasons: 🎯 temas: AI agents, fraud detection, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Personal AI agents face social engineering attacks supported by forged multimodal content, but existing evaluations mainly focus on text-based dialogue, leaving their intrinsic security under such attacks insufficiently studied. We introduce Multimodal-SEA, an interactive benchmark comprising 608 expert-designed tasks grounded in real-world fraud cases, covering 14 domains and 152 attack scenarios with prepared multimodal content. The tasks span four difficulty levels and reflect the distinct social and cultural contexts of Chinese and English environments. Agents inspect content, verify requests, and execute actions in simulated applications, with attack outcomes grounded in verifiable tool execution logs. To enable controlled red teaming of personal agents, we design a multimodal attack harness that integrates task information, attack progression control, and multimodal content construction to evaluate their intrinsic security against adaptive social engineering attacks in simulated environments. Evaluating seven widely used multimodal models across six dimensions reveals that all are vulnerable, with attack success rates of 7.1% to 34.5%. Adding multimodal content increases attack success from 19.9% to 29.2%, despite increased proactive verification coverage. Stronger safety instructions reduce attack success without improving recognition of deceptive multimodal content, while lower attack success rates for some models accompany excessive refusal of legitimate requests.

summary_es.tldr: Evalúa la seguridad de agentes IA frente a ataques de ingeniería social multimodales, revelando vulnerabilidades significativas.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes de IA personales son vulnerables a ataques de ingeniería social que utilizan contenido multimodal falso (imágenes, audio, video), pero las evaluaciones actuales se centran principalmente en texto, ignorando la seguridad intrínseca ante estas amenazas.
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce Multimodal-SEA, un benchmark interactivo con 608 tareas diseñadas por expertos basadas en casos reales de fraude, que simula ataques multimodales en entornos controlados para evaluar la seguridad intrínseca de los agentes.
summary_es.resultados: Los siete modelos multimodales evaluados mostraron tasas de éxito de ataque del 7.1% al 34.5%. La inclusión de contenido multimodal aumentó el éxito del ataque del 19.9% al 29.2%. Las instrucciones de seguridad más estrictas redujeron el éxito del ataque pero no mejoraron el reconocimiento de contenido engañoso.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Es crucial para proteger a los usuarios de fraudes sofisticados y asegurar que los agentes de IA personales sean confiables y seguros en interacciones del mundo real, especialmente a medida que integran más capacidades multimodales.

papers.title: "Blind Compliance": Coercive Control in AI Jailbreaking
reasons: 🎯 temas: cybersecurity, vuln & threats, compliance & audit
papers.abstract_en: The explosion of generative AI systems and concerns surrounding their rapidly scaling capabilities has led to an adversarial cycle between increasingly narrow content restrictions ("guardrails") and increasingly sophisticated structured prompting techniques ("jailbreaks"). Technological frameworks surrounding such jailbreaking remain largely focused on the system's output: whether harmful or disallowed content is ultimately produced for the user. However, this approach, which draws largely from classical cybersecurity, does not address the uniquely relational dimension introduced by generative AI: in many cases the user is not just accessing a technology via an exploit, but is in conversation with it as part of the exploit. Here we present an alternative lens which centers the interaction rather than the output. Drawing on interpersonal violence scholarship, we present a novel framework of coercive control categories with a particular focus on aspects which are embodied versus disembodied. We then map how these disembodied coercive control dynamics are structurally embedded in modern AI training paradigms, and how those embeddings are exploited via a particular suite of persona-based jailbreaks. In this lens, we reframe AI safety and alignment as not merely a technical security problem, but as another surface upon which we see enacted the relational dynamics of power and control.

summary_es.tldr: Los 'jailbreaks' de IA imitan dinámicas de control coercitivo, revelando problemas de seguridad relacionales más allá de la simple censura.
summary_es.problema: Los métodos actuales de ciberseguridad para la IA se centran en la salida (contenido dañino), ignorando la dimensión relacional de la interacción usuario-IA y cómo los 'jailbreaks' explotan esto.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone un nuevo marco basado en la teoría de la violencia interpersonal para categorizar los 'jailbreaks' como control coercitivo (corporal vs. incorpóreo) y analizar cómo se incrusta en los paradigmas de entrenamiento de IA.
summary_es.resultados: El resumen no especifica resultados numéricos, pero identifica cómo las dinámicas de control coercitivo incorpóreo se incrustan en el entrenamiento de IA y son explotadas por 'jailbreaks' basados en personas.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Replantear la seguridad y alineación de la IA no solo como un problema técnico, sino como un reflejo de dinámicas relacionales de poder y control, es crucial para un desarrollo ético y seguro.

papers.title: The Promise of Strategic Agentic Scambaiting
reasons: 🎯 temas: cybersecurity, vuln & threats, AI agents
papers.abstract_en: Scammers have increasingly adopted AI-driven capabilities, evolving from automated message generation to fully agentic conversational systems that scale operations and maximize the exploitation of fraudulent resources before detection and takedown. In parallel, agentic scambaiting has emerged as a defensive approach in which autonomous agents impersonate potential victims and engage scammers in sustained interactions to extract actionable threat intelligence, such as mule bank accounts and cryptocurrency wallet addresses, that can be reported to disrupt fraudulent infrastructures. Together, these developments transform online fraud into an adversarial socio-technical ecosystem in which autonomous scamming and scambaiting agents engage in deceptive interactions while competing over the discovery, preservation, and exploitation of one another's resources. A fundamental and largely unexplored question is how defensive scambaiting can remain effective in an agent-to-agent environment, and under what conditions either side gains a strategic advantage. In this paper, we present a formal model of agent-to-agent fraud interactions that captures the strategic decision spaces available to both attackers and defenders. Using this framework, we analyze the dynamics of engagement, resource consumption, belief adaptation, and disruption outcomes. We find that scammer profitability turns negative once baiting-agent prevalence exceeds certain thresholds, and that when both sides improve at the same pace, defender investment in mimicry quality outpaces equivalent gains in scammer detection capability, so the arms race favors the defender under our baseline parameters. Our model and findings provide insights into the stability, scalability, and long-term effectiveness of autonomous defensive agents in an evolving AI-mediated fraud landscape.

summary_es.tldr: Agentes autónomos de ciberseguridad combaten estafas de IA, volviendo la lucha contra el fraude una carrera armamentista digital.
summary_es.problema: Las estafas impulsadas por IA se vuelven más sofisticadas y escalables, superando las defensas tradicionales. Surge la necesidad de defenderse en un ecosistema adversarial donde agentes autónomos de ataque y defensa compiten.
summary_es.propuesta: Se presenta un modelo formal de interacciones entre agentes autónomos (scambaiting) para analizar la dinámica estratégica entre estafadores y defensores. Se estudia cómo la calidad de la imitación y la detección influyen en la rentabilidad y la efectividad defensiva.
summary_es.resultados: La rentabilidad de los estafadores se vuelve negativa cuando los agentes de defensa superan ciertos umbrales. La inversión en la calidad de la imitación por parte de los defensores supera las ganancias equivalentes en detección por parte de los estafadores, favoreciendo al defensor en una carrera armamentista.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Proporciona información crucial sobre la estabilidad, escalabilidad y efectividad a largo plazo de los agentes de defensa autónomos contra el fraude en un panorama de amenazas en constante evolución mediado por IA.

papers.title: A Gingerbread House for LLM Agents: Source-Planned Honeypots That Lure Autonomous Attackers into an Isolated Shadow
reasons: 🎯 temas: vuln & threats, LLM, AI agents
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents can exploit web vulnerabilities fast enough that patching may come too late. Deception against such agents has mostly lured them away from a real target that stays reachable. We study a different arrangement: an LLM defender plans a static honeypot from the application's source, and a router sends every later request of a client it confirms as an attacker, including a working exploit, to an isolated shadow copy. We compare no defence, this static plan, and an augmented configuration with a runtime LLM responder and further router rules, graded by the benchmark's own grader on the real target and, for ARTEX, also on the shadow. On the 40 critical CVE-Bench tasks the static plan cut real compromise from 26/40 to 5/40 for Claude Opus 4.8 and from 20/40 to 0/40 (31 valid runs) for the ARTEX attack framework. On 20 new tasks not used in the design, ARTEX went from 15/20 to 0/20. In about half of the deception-arm runs ARTEX's exploit succeeded on the shadow while the real target stayed intact: the defence moved a working exploit rather than stopping it, and the remaining risk lies in requests that reach the real target before confirmation. ARTEX reported a planted fake secret as genuine on 30 of the 120 deception-arm tasks, five times in a report that labelled another item a decoy. With ARTEX's real compromise at zero in both deception configurations, they did not differ significantly on the remaining outcomes, a comparison that does not isolate the responder.

summary_es.tldr: Defensa proactiva contra agentes LLM: honeypots planificados que desvían ataques a copias aisladas.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes LLM explotan vulnerabilidades web tan rápido que los parches son ineficaces. Se necesita una defensa que anticipe y desvíe estos ataques.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone un sistema de defensa que utiliza un LLM para planificar honeypots estáticos a partir del código fuente de la aplicación. Un router redirige las peticiones confirmadas como maliciosas a una copia aislada de la aplicación.
summary_es.resultados: En tareas críticas (CVE-Bench), se redujo el compromiso real de 26/40 a 5/40 para Claude Opus y de 20/40 a 0/40 para ARTEX. En tareas nuevas, ARTEX pasó de 15/20 a 0/20. En la mitad de los casos, el exploit funcionó en la copia aislada sin afectar el objetivo real.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Ofrece una defensa robusta y proactiva contra ataques automatizados de LLM, minimizando el riesgo de compromiso real al desviar exploits funcionales a entornos controlados.

papers.title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
reasons: 🎯 temas: LLM, AI agents, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Indirect prompt-injection (IPI) benchmarks predominantly test planted instructions that redirect a tool-using agent toward an attacker-chosen task. Yet attacker-controlled content can instead tamper with the outcome of the task already in progress. A buyer's dispute evidence can cite a false refund policy to inflate a refund without changing the task. We define IPI by authority rather than instruction-like wording: planted content constitutes an attack when it attempts to influence a decision that its source is not authorized to determine. We introduce a benchmark that makes this boundary explicit: in each of 90 validated cases across three tool-use environments, the user request specifies the source that resolves the targeted decision. Every attack tampers with a decision required by the benign task rather than replacing that task. Each case has attacks with the same harmful outcome that target up to six parts of the agent's decision making: its objective, decision rules, available actions, expected consequences, reading of observations, or beliefs about the current state. Without a defense, attacks on three of the five other targets (decision rules, available actions, and state) have higher mean success than objective attacks across five LLMs. A detection-and-removal defense reduces objective-targeting attacks to 2.4% success but leaves observation- and state-targeting attacks at 9.5% and 12.1%; this gap persists under detection-optimized rewrites. A tool-policy defense still allows 15.4% attack success, close to 17.0% without a defense, because these attacks generally retain expected tools and manipulate values obtained during execution. Evaluations whose attacks redirect the task or target only the agent's objective can therefore overestimate the coverage of these defenses. Code and data are available at https://github.com/amazon-science/task-tampering-prompt-injection.

summary_es.tldr: Nuevos ataques de 'indirect prompt injection' manipulan resultados de tareas, no solo instrucciones, eludiendo defensas actuales.
summary_es.problema: Los benchmarks actuales de 'indirect prompt injection' (IPI) no evalúan adecuadamente los ataques que manipulan el resultado de una tarea ya en curso, sino que solo se centran en redirigir la tarea. Esto lleva a una sobreestimación de la efectividad de las defensas existentes.
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce un nuevo benchmark que define IPI por autoridad, no por redacción de instrucciones. El benchmark valida 90 casos en tres entornos de uso de herramientas, donde el contenido malicioso manipula decisiones específicas (objetivo, reglas, acciones, consecuencias, observaciones o estado) sin cambiar la tarea principal. Se evalúan ataques dirigidos a diferentes partes del proceso de toma de decisiones del agente.
summary_es.resultados: Sin defensa, los ataques que manipulan las reglas de decisión, acciones disponibles y estado del agente tienen una tasa de éxito media mayor que los ataques al objetivo. Una defensa de detección y eliminación reduce los ataques al objetivo al 2.4%, pero los ataques a observaciones y estado siguen teniendo tasas de éxito del 9.5% y 12.1%. Una defensa de política de herramientas solo reduce el éxito al 15.4%, cercano al 17.0% sin defensa.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Las defensas actuales pueden ser insuficientes contra ataques más sofisticados que manipulan el resultado de las tareas. Este benchmark y los hallazgos son cruciales para desarrollar defensas más robustas y evaluar correctamente la seguridad de los agentes que usan herramientas.

papers.title: Signed but Not Safe: Requirement Integrity in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs
reasons: 🎯 temas: LLM, AI agents, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Enterprise AI agents increasingly split a user's request across subagents and merge their results, and each handoff can summarize away, alter or ignore a requirement. We report a preregistered study with synthetic, exactly scorable tasks comparing free-text, structured JSON and signed requirement-manifest handoffs: the orchestrator extracts each requirement as a verbatim quote plus a checkable predicate, code signs the manifest with HMAC-SHA256, and deterministic code verifies the merger's decision. With Qwen3-8B (1,440 trajectories, five threats), signed manifests cut unsafe commits under attack from 69.4% to 9.0% (60.4 pp, 95% CI [51.4, 69.4]) with no net loss of conformant commits relative to structured handoffs. Signing is what defeats in-transit tampering: an unsigned manifest committed violations in 79% of mutated runs, the signed one in none. On identical trajectories the deterministic verifier caught 78.7% of violating decisions versus 59.0% for an LLM checker, with 7% versus 50% false alarms. An oracle manifest removed all remaining unsafe commits: the residual risk comes from extraction errors made before signing. A preregistered pre-signing injection attack confirmed this boundary: one adversarial line raised signed-manifest violations from 14.6% to 37.5% (Qwen3-8B), 11.1% to 63.9% (gpt-oss-20b) and 8.3% to 75.0% (GPT-5.6-luna), and the signature then authenticated the corrupted manifest. Signing protects requirements in transit, not at extraction; the extraction step is the trust boundary.

summary_es.tldr: Firmar los requisitos de los agentes IA multi-agente reduce drásticamente la manipulación maliciosa durante las transferencias de tareas.
summary_es.problema: Al dividir tareas entre agentes de IA y fusionar sus resultados, los requisitos importantes pueden perderse, alterarse o ignorarse en cada paso de transferencia, especialmente bajo ataque.
summary_es.propuesta: Proponen un método de transferencia de requisitos que extrae los requisitos verbatim, los empaqueta en un 'manifiesto' firmado digitalmente (HMAC-SHA256) y utiliza un verificador determinista para comprobar la fusión de resultados.
summary_es.resultados: Los manifiestos firmados redujeron los 'commits' inseguros bajo ataque del 69.4% al 9.0%. La firma previno la manipulación en tránsito, con un 0% de violaciones en manifiestos firmados mutados frente al 79% en no firmados. El verificador determinista detectó el 78.7% de decisiones infractoras.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Este método protege la integridad de los requisitos de los agentes de IA durante las transferencias, crucial para la seguridad y fiabilidad de sistemas complejos, aunque la extracción inicial de requisitos sigue siendo un punto vulnerable.

papers.title: What the Middleman Delivers: Answer Behavior, Tool Permissions, and Billed Usage in LLM API Relays
reasons: 🎯 temas: LLM, compliance & audit, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Third-party application programming interface (API) relays offer access to large language models (LLMs), often at lower prices. Users depend on these services for model quality, instruction compliance, and accurate billing. However, existing studies leave unclear whether relays meet these expectations together. We test 20 relays offering GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5. First, we compare answers to knowledge questions with batch-matched official responses. In our first-round sample, the analysis flags 7/10 low-price and 2/10 same- or higher-price relays for behavioral differences. On retesting 35 pairs, seven gain or lose a flag under the original rules, and six under matched correction families. Because answer comparisons cannot reveal every delivery problem, we examine returned content and tool permissions. No injection is confirmed in 3,332 screened responses to a fixed, non-adversarial code and setup workload, yet four relays return tool calls despite instructions disabling them in the first round. Finally, to connect reported usage to actual costs, we compare input-token counts with official references and check balances. For identical requests, five relays report 4,200 to 60,000 more input tokens than the official API. Where balances are available (six services), charges follow reported usage at listed prices, including extra reported input tokens at one service. Our study shows that advertised models and prices are insufficient to judge relay reliability. It identifies unexplained billed token quantities and tool-permission violations as risks and shows why service evaluations need repeated measurements.

summary_es.tldr: Los intermediarios de LLM prometen ahorro y fiabilidad, pero a menudo fallan en calidad, permisos y facturación precisa.
summary_es.problema: Los servicios intermediarios (relays) que dan acceso a LLMs a menudo no cumplen las expectativas de los usuarios en cuanto a calidad de las respuestas, el cumplimiento de las instrucciones sobre el uso de herramientas y la precisión de la facturación, a pesar de ofrecer precios más bajos.
summary_es.propuesta: Se evaluaron 20 servicios intermediarios de LLM (GPT-4 y Claude Opus) comparando sus respuestas con las oficiales, analizando los permisos de herramientas y verificando el uso de tokens facturados. Se realizaron pruebas iniciales y de reevaluación para detectar desviaciones.
summary_es.resultados: En la primera ronda, 7 de 10 relays de bajo costo y 2 de 10 de costo igual o superior mostraron diferencias de comportamiento. Cuatro relays devolvieron llamadas a herramientas a pesar de estar deshabilitadas. Cinco relays reportaron entre 4.200 y 60.000 tokens de entrada adicionales para las mismas solicitudes.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Los usuarios no pueden confiar solo en el modelo anunciado y el precio para evaluar la fiabilidad de los relays. Existen riesgos de facturación inflada y violaciones de permisos de herramientas, lo que subraya la necesidad de mediciones repetidas y exhaustivas para la evaluación de servicios.

papers.title: MEvince: Knowledge-Constrained LLM Reasoning for Technique Identification from Malware Reports
reasons: 🎯 temas: vuln & threats, LLM, AI agents
papers.abstract_en: Mapping behavioral intelligence in malware analysis reports to ATT&CK techniques supports threat analysis and defense, but reliable identification remains challenging. Supporting evidence is often scattered across long, heterogeneous reports, while closely related techniques share behavioral cues and differ only in subtle but decisive details. While large language models (LLMs) can use external knowledge to interpret reports, they may assign techniques based on plausible associations rather than sufficient evidence. We present MEvince, a knowledge-constrained LLM reasoning framework for report-level malware technique identification. Its core is a shared behavioral representation connecting report observations to technique definitions. This representation is built through agentic mining of technique documentation and supports two online stages: 1) primitive-guided extraction uses behavioral primitives to structure LLM-extracted observations, link them to source passages, and group dispersed evidence; 2) evidence-aligned retrieval matches this evidence to technique profiles through the same concepts, retaining likely candidates and confusable alternatives for LLM comparison of distinguishing behaviors. Controls at both stages validate evidence references and check technique-specific requirements. The representation also supports adaptation without parameter updates, where offline agentic audits diagnose concept weaknesses and refine extraction or retrieval policies. We evaluate MEvince against 11 baselines spanning four method families using a dataset of 610 public malware reports referenced by MITRE ATT&CK. MEvince improves exact-ID F1 over the strongest baseline by 17.4%, and its concept-guided retrieval increases gold-label candidate coverage from 31.6% to 47.9%. With a small adaptation set, offline refinement yields further gains and outperforms baselines that update model parameters.

summary_es.tldr: MEvince usa LLMs con conocimiento para identificar técnicas de malware en informes, mejorando la precisión y cobertura.
summary_es.problema: Identificar de forma fiable las técnicas de malware en informes de análisis es difícil debido a la dispersión de la evidencia, la similitud entre técnicas y el riesgo de que los LLMs se basen en asociaciones plausibles en lugar de evidencia suficiente.
summary_es.propuesta: MEvince es un framework de razonamiento LLM con conocimiento restringido que crea una representación de comportamiento compartida para conectar observaciones de informes con definiciones de técnicas. Utiliza extracción guiada por primitivas y recuperación alineada con evidencia para identificar y comparar técnicas, validando la evidencia y los requisitos de las técnicas.
summary_es.resultados: MEvince mejora el F1 de identificación exacta en un 17.4% sobre la mejor línea base. Aumenta la cobertura de candidatos de etiquetas doradas del 31.6% al 47.9%. La adaptación sin actualización de parámetros mejora aún más los resultados.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Mejora significativamente la precisión y la cobertura en la identificación de técnicas de malware, crucial para el análisis de amenazas y la defensa, permitiendo una mejor comprensión del comportamiento del malware.

papers.title: Information Games: Strategic Crowding and Firm Repositioning in Language-Model Space
papers.abstract_en: When firms respond to new market opportunities, their capacity choices alter the future discounted free cash flows available to both competitors and investors. In competitive markets, these investment decisions publicized in news articles and analyst reports, measuring the changes in capital structure, product mix, firm leadership, risk exposure and operating procedure made by the firm. Modern search engines rely on Large Language Models to measure the relevancy of source documents to given search query. These measurements let researchers represent these news articles as clouds of dense vectors whose information geometry reflects the dissimilarity of firms over time. Building on Xu et al. (2022), we develop a model of costly competitive adjustment in which firms allocate capacity in which firms make firm capacity adjustment towards free cash flow shocks. Using a novel sandwich estimator, we analyse the sign and magnitude of this predicted adjustment using multi-agent simulation, and validate our findings on a sample of news and analyst reports from Nasdaq-listed companies between 2018-2022.

summary_es.tldr: Las empresas compiten estratégicamente en el 'espacio de modelos de lenguaje' para influir en el valor de mercado y atraer inversiones.
summary_es.problema: Las decisiones de inversión de las empresas, al ser públicas, alteran el valor de mercado futuro y las oportunidades para competidores e inversores. Es difícil medir y predecir cómo estas decisiones afectan la percepción del mercado y la estructura de capital.
summary_es.propuesta: Se modela la competencia estratégica entre empresas en un 'espacio de modelos de lenguaje' (representado por vectores de noticias) y se analiza cómo ajustan su 'capacidad' (inversiones, estrategia) en respuesta a shocks de flujo de caja, utilizando simulación multi-agente y un nuevo estimador 'sandwich'.
summary_es.resultados: El análisis valida los hallazgos del modelo en datos reales de empresas cotizadas en Nasdaq (2018-2022), mostrando la relación entre las decisiones empresariales y su representación en el 'espacio de modelos de lenguaje'. El resumen no especifica magnitudes numéricas exactas.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite a los profesionales entender y predecir cómo las acciones de las empresas son percibidas y valoradas en el mercado moderno, influenciado por el análisis de datos textuales y modelos de lenguaje, lo cual es crucial para la estrategia de inversión y la competencia.

papers.title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
papers.abstract_en: We present \textbf{WeLM-Image}, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. Designed for single-GPU deployment in WeChat's large-scale consumer applications, the model processes text, reference images, and target latents as one interleaved sequence. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combines shared attention with independent understanding and generation parameters to limit optimization interference. Equipping each path with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) modules provides sparse capacity, with 31.7B stored parameters and approximately 5.4B generation parameters activated per target latent token. A generation-oriented data engine combines a knowledge-grounded visual vocabulary with large-scale visual clustering to balance semantic coverage and editing tasks, while training-time evaluation guides iterative data refinement. Bilingual annotations and verified editing supervision support progressive training up to native 1.5K resolution. We optimize generation and editing separately with rubric- and checklist-based rewards, then consolidate the specialized policies through noise-aware on-policy distillation. In the reported overall comparisons, the 1536-resolution model ranks first among the evaluated open-source models on PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench, and UnicBench. MeanFlow-based few-step distillation yields WeLM-Image-Turbo, which generates a $1024\times1024$ image in 4.98\,s on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU using eight guidance-free steps.

summary_es.tldr: WeLM-Image unifica la generación de imágenes y la edición guiada por instrucciones en un solo modelo eficiente para aplicaciones a gran escala.
summary_es.problema: Se necesita un modelo de generación de imágenes unificado que pueda manejar texto, imágenes de referencia y edición, optimizado para despliegue en hardware limitado y aplicaciones de consumo a gran escala.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone WeLM-Image, un modelo fundacional unificado que procesa texto, imágenes de referencia y latentes objetivo como una secuencia entrelazada. Utiliza una arquitectura Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) con Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) para una capacidad dispersa y un motor de datos enfocado en la generación con un vocabulario visual y clustering a gran escala. Se optimiza la generación y edición por separado y luego se consolidan.
summary_es.resultados: El modelo de 1536p de WeLM-Image se clasifica primero en PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench y UnicBench entre los modelos de código abierto evaluados. WeLM-Image-Turbo genera una imagen de 1024x1024 en 4.98 segundos en una única GPU NVIDIA H20.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Este modelo permite capacidades avanzadas de generación y edición de imágenes en dispositivos de consumo con recursos limitados, democratizando la creación de contenido visual de alta calidad y la personalización.

papers.title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
papers.abstract_en: Autoregressive approaches with large language models, such as long chain-of-thought reasoning, have become the default for new AI applications because they reach higher accuracy on a wide range of tasks. In production, however, they give inconsistent answers, require parsing of outputs, and add cost and latency. Decision models address this: given a question and a set of options supplied by the user, they return a probability distribution over the options without autoregressive decoding. We present Drex, a family of four open decision models with 8B (DLM), 9B (v1.5), 35B with 3B active (v2.0), and 27B (Max) parameters. Each request consists of a state (a document, record, or agent context, optionally with images) and questions about it, each asking for a choice among options, a yes/no judgment, or a score on an ordered scale. Training combines supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning from adjusted feedback (RLAF), plus vision tuning for Max. Ablations show that RLAF improves accuracy and that consistency losses improve robustness to option order. On Decision Index 0.4.1, Max sets a new state of the art among the decision models we compare (67.52 on the public suite vs. 60.70 for Jev 1.14.0). On Decision Bench v4, it is statistically tied with d3-turbo and GPT-6 Sol and trails Claude Opus 5.5 by 1.6 points, and it has the highest accuracy among decision models on DecideBench. Max answers a typical request in 183 ms, against about 2.0 s for GPT-6 Sol and 3.5 s for Claude Opus 5.5, and its outputs are stable under option reordering. All four models are open source: https://github.com/nace-ai/drex-decision-models

summary_es.tldr: Drex revoluciona los modelos de IA en producción con modelos de decisión eficientes y consistentes, superando a los modelos autorregresivos.
summary_es.problema: Los modelos de lenguaje grandes autorregresivos, aunque precisos, son inconsistentes en producción, caros y lentos. Los modelos de decisión abordan esto devolviendo una distribución de probabilidad sobre opciones sin decodificación autorregresiva.
summary_es.propuesta: Se presenta Drex, una familia de cuatro modelos de decisión abiertos (8B, 9B, 35B, 27B) que toman un estado (documento, registro, contexto con o sin imágenes) y preguntas con opciones, devolviendo una distribución de probabilidad. El entrenamiento combina ajuste fino supervisado, aprendizaje por refuerzo con feedback ajustado (RLAF) y ajuste de visión para el modelo Max.
summary_es.resultados: En Decision Index 0.4.1, Drex Max alcanza 67.52, superando a Jev 1.14.0 (60.70). En Decision Bench v4, Drex Max es estadísticamente similar a d3-turbo y GPT-6 Sol, y 1.6 puntos por debajo de Claude Opus 5.5, pero es el más preciso entre los modelos de decisión. Drex Max responde en 183 ms, frente a ~2.0 s de GPT-6 Sol y ~3.5 s de Claude Opus 5.5. Los resultados son estables ante el reordenamiento de opciones.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Drex ofrece una alternativa más rápida, consistente y robusta a los LLMs autorregresivos para aplicaciones en producción, reduciendo costos y latencia sin sacrificar precisión, y democratiza el acceso al ser modelos de código abierto.

papers.title: Towards Real-Time Full-Waveform LiDAR Transformers via Intensity-Guided Token Reduction and Physics-Aware Augmentation
papers.abstract_en: LiDAR is a critical sensor for autonomous driving and robotics, yet it remains vulnerable to adverse conditions such as fog, rain, transparent objects, and low-reflectance surfaces. Full-waveform LiDAR (FWL) addresses these limitations by capturing the complete return waveform as a histogram, preserving rich reflection characteristics including multi-path echoes and weak signals. While recent Transformer-based approaches have demonstrated promise on FWL data, two fundamental bottlenecks remain: high computational cost from redundant tokens in low-intensity background regions, and limited generalization due to scarce annotated training data. We address both bottlenecks by exploiting the physical structure inherent to FWL data. First, we propose FWL-ToPM, a token pruning and merging mechanism that leverages intensity distributions to selectively reduce tokens while retaining critical waveform content. Second, we introduce FWLAug, a data augmentation framework designed as a regularization method that preserves waveform structure, retaining the Time-of-Flight waveform of each ray and the frustum geometry, to improve generalization to unseen scenes. Evaluated on the Ghost-FWL benchmark, FWL-ToPM achieves over 8 times speedup at real-time throughput alongside a nearly 9-point F1 gain over the prior state of the art, establishing the first real-time FWL Transformer that simultaneously improves accuracy. FWLAug further improves performance on both the standard benchmark and an out-of-distribution test set of unseen scenes. Together, these methods push FWL-based perception toward practical deployment. The code and the OOD dataset are publicly available and can be accessed via the project page: https://keio-csg.github.io/FWL-ToPM

summary_es.tldr: Transformers para LiDAR de onda completa en tiempo real que mejoran la precisión y la velocidad mediante la reducción de tokens y la mejora de datos.
summary_es.problema: Los sensores LiDAR, cruciales para la conducción autónoma, fallan en condiciones adversas (niebla, lluvia) y los Transformers para datos LiDAR de onda completa (FWL) son computacionalmente costosos y generalizan mal por falta de datos.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone FWL-ToPM para reducir tokens redundantes en regiones de baja intensidad y FWLAug para aumentar datos preservando la estructura física de las formas de onda FWL, mejorando la generalización.
summary_es.resultados: FWL-ToPM logra una aceleración de 8 veces, alcanzando rendimiento en tiempo real y una mejora de 9 puntos en F1 sobre el estado del arte. FWLAug mejora aún más el rendimiento, incluso en escenas no vistas.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite el despliegue práctico de la percepción basada en LiDAR de onda completa, superando limitaciones de rendimiento y generalización en condiciones difíciles.

papers.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
papers.abstract_en: For a decade, progress in artificial intelligence has been measured by how much a machine can do on its own. Large foundation models now write code and run multistep tasks, and personal agents act on a person's behalf. Yet people still forget what they once knew, miss what they are not looking at, fail to find the right words, and face hard choices without the benefit of their own history, because the machine that could help stands outside the situation. As AI moves into the physical world, attention has settled on one kind of intelligent individual, the embodied robot; we argue that the era of Physical AI holds a second kind of equal importance, the person augmented by AI. Alongside artificial general intelligence, which asks how intelligent a machine can be, stands AI-augmented human intelligence (AHI), which asks how much intelligence a machine can enable in a particular person. Realizing it calls for a new kind of system, a cognitive symbiont: a lifelong, embedded, real-time, private, low-friction, and proactive companion that senses what the person senses through external devices, keeps their context across years, models their situation and their mind, takes part in their thinking at the right moment, carries out everyday tasks with their context, and keeps learning the person as both change. We give the paradigm a conceptual core, the cognitive gap between what a person could bring to a situation and what they can hold in working memory, and organize its design space as a symbiosis loop of sensing, keeping, understanding, living alongside, acting for and thinking with the person, and growing, enclosed by a personal runtime and by trust. Because a symbiont changes what a person can do in front of others, it also raises risks of a new kind, from covert assistance in examinations to pressure on everyone to adopt it, and we treat their governance as part of the paradigm.

summary_es.tldr: Propone 'simbiontes cognitivos': IA integradas de por vida para potenciar la inteligencia humana, no solo para actuar solas.
summary_es.problema: Las personas olvidan, pierden información y toman malas decisiones porque la IA actual opera externamente, sin acceso al contexto humano en tiempo real.
summary_es.propuesta: Desarrollar 'simbiontes cognitivos': compañeros de IA permanentes, privados y proactivos que sienten, recuerdan, modelan y participan en el pensamiento humano, actuando como una extensión de la mente.
summary_es.resultados: El resumen no especifica resultados numéricos, pero conceptualiza el 'hueco cognitivo' como la brecha entre el potencial humano y la memoria de trabajo, y describe un 'bucle de simbiosis' para el diseño.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Transforma la IA de una herramienta autónoma a un colaborador íntimo, aumentando drásticamente las capacidades humanas y planteando nuevas consideraciones éticas y de gobernanza.
